title: ModernBERT Toxicity Model with Structural Features
summary: The solution cleans comment text and computes 16 scaled structural features covering length, casing, character ratios, punctuation, URLs, mentions, and repeated punctuation. A pretrained ModernBERT-large encoder, with gradient checkpointing, produces CLS and attention-mask mean-pooled representations; their projection is concatenated with an MLP projection of the structural features to predict one toxicity logit. Labels include soft toxicity, masked subtype and identity annotations, and hard thresholds for identity-based strata. Eligible single-identity comments may undergo constrained identity-term replacement during training. The loss combines optionally weighted soft-target binary cross-entropy with a pairwise logistic ranking loss, including overall and subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP identity comparisons; identity losses are smooth-max aggregated, and ranking has weight 0.20. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates, excluded decay parameters, mixed precision, clipping, accumulation, warm-up, and finite-loss checks. A no-replacement sampler seeks identity/label-stratified batches. Inference tokenizes truncated text, applies sigmoid probabilities, and retries with smaller batches after CUDA memory errors.

title: Dual-view sparse toxicity classifier
summary: The solution cleans comment text and creates a debiased view by replacing matched identity terms with category placeholders. It builds hashed binary word unigram/bigram features for both views, clean-text character 3–5-grams, and training-standardized numeric style features. Sparse fields are encoded by embedding-bag latent and wide paths. Debiased word and numeric features form a base representation, character features add context, and a gated bounded residual from original words is fused for the full prediction. Heads produce toxicity, subtype and identity outputs; identity prediction uses gradient reversal on contextual features. Training uses weighted BCE for full and debiased toxicity, masked weighted subtype and identity losses, consistency for non-toxic identity examples, and ranking losses overall and for subgroup, BPSN and BNSP slices. Sparse parameters use Adagrad and remaining parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped. Shuffled batches run up to three epochs. Inference returns sigmoid full-toxicity probabilities.

title: Fairness-Aware Sparse Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes comments by replacing URLs, emails, mentions and identity terms, then builds hashed word 1–2-gram, character 3–5-gram and standardized style features. Weighted EmbeddingBag components encode sparse inputs; debiased-word and numeric features provide a base representation, character features add context, and original-word features are incorporated through a sigmoid gate with a bounded residual. It predicts toxicity and optional subtype outputs, with a gradient-reversal identity classifier to encourage identity-invariant context. Training combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, non-toxic identity consistency and hard pairwise ranking losses for overall and identity slices. Slice-loss EMAs update robust weights using multiplicative updates and capped-simplex projection. Replay reservoirs supply examples missing from ranking slices. Sparse parameters use Adagrad and dense parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped and non-finite-loss batches skipped. Inference applies sigmoid to toxicity logits.

title: Dual-View Sparse Debiased Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized by decoding HTML/Unicode, masking URLs, emails and mentions, removing tags/control characters and canonicalizing simple obfuscation. The pipeline builds clean and identity-masked text, then concatenates hashed word unigram/bigram features from both views, clean character 3–5-grams, and standardized style features. A sparse neural model encodes word and character fields with weighted EmbeddingBag latent and wide-logit components. Debiased words and numeric features form a base state; characters add context, while original words contribute through a sigmoid gate and bounded residual. It predicts toxicity and subtypes, with an identity adversary connected through gradient reversal. The loss combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked weighted subtype and identity BCE, consistency between full and debiased predictions for non-toxic identity examples, and hard ranking losses for overall and identity-derived slices. Replay reservoirs add missing slice sides to training batches. Sparse parameters use Adagrad and dense parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped. Inference returns sigmoid-transformed full toxicity logits.

title: Adversarial ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text and derives 16 standardized structural features. It uses masked soft toxicity, subtype, and identity labels, thresholds hard labels at 0.5, and identifies eligible identity-term replacements. A ModernBERT-large encoder combines CLS and masked-mean token embeddings, projects semantic and structural features, and produces a toxicity logit. A gradient-reversal head predicts nine identity labels from semantic features, with masked BCE weighted toward benign comments. The objective combines soft-target BCE with sampled pairwise logistic ranking losses for overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP slices, using a smooth maximum across identity families. Training can replace identity terms, uses identity-stratified batches, AdamW groups, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, warm-up scheduling, and a step-ramped adversarial coefficient. Inference applies sigmoid and retries smaller CUDA batches after memory errors. Checkpoints include model, tokenizer, scaler, and settings.

title: Counterfactual Chunked DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, computes standardized numeric text and lexicon features, and builds soft toxicity, auxiliary subtype, and masked identity targets with toxicity/identity-aware sample weights. It augments selected identity-labelled comments through deterministic identity-term counterfactual swaps, reducing their weights. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes 256-token chunks; chunk representations combine CLS and masked learned-attention pooling, then chunk attention aggregates them. Numeric features pass through an MLP and are fused with text features. General toxicity logits are dropout-averaged; subtype and identity heads are jointly trained, and subtype mechanism weights can combine subtype probabilities with the general prediction. The objective includes weighted main BCE, masked auxiliary losses, identity-slice balanced losses, score-gap penalties, and mechanism regularization. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, checkpointing, and early stopping. Inference outputs clipped sigmoid probabilities.

title: Identity-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: A ModernBERT-large toxicity classifier combines CLS and masked mean token embeddings with standardized structural text features. Comments are conservatively cleaned; 16 features capture length, casing, character types, punctuation, URLs, emails, mentions, and repeated punctuation. Soft toxicity, subtype, and identity labels use missing-label masks, while thresholds define identity metric strata. The scalar logit is trained with weighted soft-target BCE and identity-sliced pairwise logistic ranking losses, including sampled within-batch pairs and detached per-identity historical-logit buffers. Slice losses cover subgroup, background-positive/subgroup-negative, and subgroup-positive/background-negative cases, with smooth-max identity aggregation. Eligible uniquely identified comments may receive identity-term substitutions while retaining toxicity targets and updating batch-local strata. A stratified sampler seeds batches from metric slices. AdamW uses distinct backbone/head rates, no decay for bias or normalization parameters, warmup, mixed precision, gradient accumulation and clipping. Inference applies sigmoid probabilities, with reduced batch-size retry after CUDA memory errors.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier with Structural Features
summary: Comments are conservatively cleaned, tokenized to 256 tokens, and augmented with 16 standardized structural features covering length, character ratios, punctuation, URLs, emails, and mentions. ModernBERT-large produces CLS and masked-mean embeddings; their projection is concatenated with an MLP projection of structural features and passed through dropout to a scalar logit. Training uses soft-target BCE, optionally weighted, plus sampled logistic ranking losses over overall, subgroup, and identity-related positive/negative slices, with identity-family losses combined by a smooth maximum. Hard toxicity and scored identity labels are masked when unavailable; identities are objective-only inputs. A sampler periodically seeks identity-stratified batches while covering rows without replacement. AdamW separates backbone/head learning rates, uses warmup, selective weight decay, clipping, AMP, gradient accumulation, and scheduler steps only after applied updates. Inference applies sigmoid and retries with smaller batches after CUDA OOM.

title: Chunk-attentive DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: Text is normalized (Unicode, punctuation, markup, URLs, emails and handles) and paired with standardized style, lexical, identity and hostility features. A deterministic split is used. Training weights emphasize toxic and identity-annotated examples, particularly rare identities. Selected identity examples receive hash-selected, case-preserving identity-swap counterfactuals with transformed identity labels and 0.70 weight. Long text retains beginning and end around a middle marker. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large encoder, with only its top eight layers trainable, uses first-token plus masked attention pooling, chunk attention, numeric-feature MLP fusion, and dropout-averaged toxicity heads; subtype and identity heads are auxiliary. Final toxicity combines general and subtype non-toxicity through learned nonnegative weights. The loss includes weighted main BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, identity subgroup/background smooth-max terms, identity probability-gap penalties, and mechanism regularization. AdamW, warmup-cosine scheduling, AMP, accumulation, clipping and finite-value checks are used. Inference outputs clipped finite sigmoid probabilities.

title: Slice-aware DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: Comments undergo Unicode, HTML, punctuation and placeholder normalization, then standardized numeric feature extraction. Training data is split before fitting transforms. Identity-annotated rows can generate deterministic hash-selected counterfactual identity-word swaps, retaining targets and features but using swapped identity labels and 0.70 weight. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder with frozen embeddings/lower layers pools CLS and attention-weighted tokens; valid chunks are attention-combined. Projected numeric features are fused with text features. Heads predict toxicity, subtypes and identities; four dropout toxicity passes are averaged, and learned positive subtype weights may combine probabilities. The loss includes weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, smooth-max balanced subgroup/BPSN/BNSP slice losses, gap penalties and weight regularization. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, selective decay, AMP, checkpointing, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine scheduling. Inference applies identical preprocessing, sigmoid outputs and probability clipping.

title: Dual-view latent-rationale toxicity classifier
summary: The solution normalizes text, replaces entities such as URLs and mentions with special tokens, and derives numeric style, abuse, identity and discourse features. It creates primary text and a quote-masked alternate view, standardizes numeric features on training data, and weights examples for duplicates and annotator counts. A ModernBERT encoder, extended with custom tokens, produces token embeddings. Evidence and relevance heads generate token toxicity scores and masked attention, whose weighted embedding is fused with the first-token representation and numeric-feature tower. Global and bag-level toxicity logits are combined through a learned gate; additional heads predict beta-binomial concentration and subtypes. Training uses weighted beta-binomial and binary losses, bag and subtype losses, subgroup disparity regularization, alternate-view consistency, and gate regularization. AdamW applies layerwise backbone learning-rate decay, warmup/cosine scheduling, AMP, accumulation and clipping. Length-grouped shuffled batches are used. Inference averages primary and changed alternate-view probabilities, then sanitizes and clips outputs.

title: Dual-View Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution predicts toxicity probabilities from paired original and identity-masked comments plus standardized numeric text features. Comments are normalized for markup, whitespace, URLs, emails, mentions and controls; a fixed identity lexicon is replaced with an identity token in the masked view. It derives 22 stylistic features, fits scaling only on training data, uses clipped soft toxicity labels, and constructs subtype, identity and counterfactual metadata. A partially fine-tuned ModernBERT-large encodes both 256-token views; first-token and masked-mean pooling are combined. A GELU numeric encoder and gated dual-view fusion produce toxicity, subtype and gradient-reversed identity predictions. Training uses weighted toxicity BCE, branch BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, adversarial identity BCE, view consistency, pairwise ranking, and worst-group ranking losses. AdamW applies separate backbone/head settings, AMP, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, warmup-cosine scheduling, and partial-window correction. Inference tokenizes paired views, applies sigmoid to main logits, and clips outputs to [0,1].

title: Sparse Wide-Deep Toxicity Predictor
summary: Comment text is normalized by replacing URLs, emails, IP addresses and usernames, then represented with hashed word 1–2-grams, character 3–5-grams, and standardized dense style, lexical, identity and context features. CSR features are converted to embedding-bag indices, values and offsets. A wide sparse logit and normalized, dropout-regularized deep pooled embeddings are combined with an optional dense tower and shared GELU layers. Heads predict toxicity, subtypes and identities; a gradient-reversed adversarial identity head uses toxicity features and the wide logit. Training uses fractional toxicity labels, cell-balanced and uncertainty-aware sample weights, and batches augmented from identity-by-binary-toxicity cells. Losses include weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCEs, adversarial BCE, representation decorrelation, and subgroup/BPSN/BNSP ranking losses with soft worst-group aggregation. Embeddings use Adagrad; remaining parameters use AdamW, warmup-cosine schedules, adversarial ramping and gradient clipping. Inference sigmoids and clips toxicity probabilities.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system cleans toxicity comments, tokenizes them with ModernBERT-large, and derives standardized numeric text and lexicon features. Identity spans detected from token offsets are removed in a neutral pooling mask. A partially fine-tuned ModernBERT encodes tokens once; original and neutral pooled views are gated, fused with an MLP representation of numeric features, and projected to toxicity logits. Auxiliary heads predict toxicity subtypes and identities, with gradient reversal for identity-adversarial training. Identity-conditioned batches balance toxic/non-toxic subgroup and background examples. Training uses weighted soft-label BCE, view consistency, ranking surrogates, and smooth worst-group losses. Only the final backbone layers and normalization are trainable. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates, warmup followed by cosine decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and gradient clipping. Inference applies sigmoid and clips toxicity probabilities.

title: Dual-View Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The pipeline cleans comments and creates an identity-masked text view. It derives standardized text statistics, fitting the scaler on training data only, and retains soft toxicity, subtype, and identity labels. A partially fine-tuned ModernBERT encodes original and masked text; pooled representations and a GELU numeric-feature encoder are fused through a gated counterfactual representation for toxicity and subtype prediction. A gradient-reversal identity head promotes identity-invariant features. The loss combines weighted soft-label toxicity BCE, view-specific BCE, masked subtype/identity BCE, counterfactual consistency, and pairwise ranking losses for overall and identity-related groups with smooth worst-group aggregation. Epoch-seeded identity-quadrant sampling balances subgroup/background and positive/negative examples. AdamW uses separate backbone and head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, AMP, gradient accumulation, clipping, and checkpointing. Inference batches indexed examples, applies sigmoid to main logits, and clips probabilities to [0,1].

title: Identity-aware DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: The model tokenizes comment text and combines DeBERTa-v3-large representations with numeric features. It uses pooled non-identity evidence and an identity-aware branch based on detected identity-token spans and surrounding context, then predicts toxicity alongside auxiliary, evidence and concentration outputs. Training data include soft toxicity labels, masked auxiliary labels, annotator counts, identity/context values and sample weights. Metric-cell-balanced sortish sampling uses approximate sequence length, targets and identity groups. The joint criterion consumes primary, concentration, auxiliary, sentence-evidence and token-evidence logits, corresponding labels and masks, identity-token masks, annotator counts and weights. Mixed-precision optimization accumulates gradients, clips their norm to 1.0 and uses AdamW-style updates with warmup followed by cosine learning-rate decay. At inference, logits are sigmoid-transformed and clipped; CUDA out-of-memory errors trigger a reduced-batch retry. Validation computes overall, subgroup, BPSN and BNSP AUC diagnostics.

title: Dual-view bias-aware ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: Comments are split before preprocessing, then cleaned with placeholder tokens for URLs, emails and mentions. The system builds an identity-masked text view and 22 normalized style/lexicon features, fitting the feature scaler on training data only. Soft toxicity labels, subtype and identity labels, and weighted samples emphasize toxic and identity-related cases. A shared pretrained ModernBERT encodes original and masked texts; most backbone layers are frozen. First-token and attention-masked mean pooling form text embeddings, while an MLP encodes numeric features. A learned gate fuses masked representations with original-minus-masked differences and an absolute-difference correction. Toxicity, subtype and gradient-reversed identity heads are trained using weighted BCE, view consistency, pairwise ranking, and subgroup/BPSN/BNSP ranking losses. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, AMP, accumulation, clipping, warm-up and cosine decay. Inference tokenizes both views, applies the feature scaler, and returns clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Fairness-Aware Sparse Toxicity Classification
summary: Comments are normalized into hashed word 1–2-gram and character 3–5-gram sparse features, with standardized engineered text features. Sparse embedding-bag and pooled embedding branches, optionally combined with dense features, output toxicity logits and auxiliary subtype and identity predictions. Training uses continuous toxicity targets and masked subtype/identity labels. The objective combines weighted soft-label toxicity BCE, subgroup/BPSN/BNSP margin-ranking surrogates, auxiliary BCE, gradient-reversal identity adversarial training, and toxicity–identity representation orthogonality. Weights reflect identity–toxicity cell frequency, label uncertainty, and annotator count. Identity-cell batches can apply counterfactual identity-term substitutions while retaining toxicity targets and updating identities. Dense parameters use AdamW and sparse embeddings use Adagrad, with warmup/cosine schedules, adversarial ramping, and dense-gradient clipping. Training uses separate optimizers, then finalizes evaluation/checkpoint handling and test prediction export. Inference returns clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Identity-Excluded DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution preprocesses toxicity comments with Unicode and entity normalization, replacement markers for URLs, emails and mentions, pragmatic regex features, identity/context detection, and optional context prefixes. Numeric features are standardized using training data only. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder, with only its last up-to-eight layers unfrozen, encodes truncated text; identity-token states are excluded from main evidence pooling and direct numeric identity inputs. Non-identity states yield attention-pooled evidence features fused with projected numeric features for toxicity, auxiliary-label and concentration predictions. An identity branch uses identity and nearby non-identity states for a gated bounded residual toxicity correction. Training combines reliability-weighted soft BCE, beta-binomial vote likelihood, pairwise ranking, masked auxiliary BCE, evidence BCE and identity-token evidence regularization. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Evaluation/inference applies sigmoid and clipped probabilities, preserves order, handles OOM by reducing batch size, and reports subgroup AUC diagnostics.

title: Context-aware DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: The pipeline normalizes comment text and derives pragmatic numeric features from surface statistics, lexical cues, identity terms, and identity-context interactions. It builds optional natural-language context prefixes, truncates long text by retaining both ends, and creates soft toxicity, masked auxiliary, identity, and annotator-count targets. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder is fine-tuned in its last encoder layers with gradient checkpointing. Identity phrase tokens are masked from learned evidence attention; remaining token representations are pooled and fused with numeric features and evidence statistics. Heads predict toxicity, auxiliary labels, evidence aggregates, and beta-binomial concentration. Sample weights account for identity/toxicity cells and label reliability. Training uses masked-token augmentation, length-sorted shuffled batches, AdamW with separate backbone/head rates, warmup then cosine decay, mixed precision, accumulation, and gradient clipping. The loss combines weighted soft-label BCE, beta-binomial count likelihood, pairwise ranking, masked auxiliary BCE, evidence BCE, and identity-evidence regularization. Inference sigmoid-transforms and clips logits, reducing batch size after CUDA OOM.

title: Fairness-Aware Sparse Wide-and-Deep Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, then builds hashed word 1–2-gram and character 3–5-gram sparse features plus standardized dense style, lexical, identity and interaction features. A sparse wide-and-deep network uses embedding-bag pooling for a linear wide logit and learned sparse embeddings, concatenated with a dense GELU/dropout pathway. It predicts toxicity with auxiliary subtype and identity heads; a gradient-reversal identity head is trained from toxicity features and the wide logit. Toxicity uses weighted soft-label BCE, while masked BCE supervises available auxiliary labels. Additional losses penalize toxicity/identity representation correlation and apply identity-group ranking constraints. Weights account for identity-toxicity cell frequency, near-threshold labels and optional annotator counts. Batches are augmented with samples from each nonempty identity-by-binary-toxicity cell. Dense parameters use AdamW, embeddings use Adagrad, with warm-up/cosine learning rates, increasing adversarial strength and dense-gradient clipping. Inference applies sigmoid to the combined toxicity logit and clips finite predictions to [0,1].

title: Fairness-Aware Counterfactual Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes comments, tokenizes emails, URLs, IP addresses and handles, creates identity-masked counterfactual texts, and derives scaled style features. It constructs soft and binary toxicity targets, identity memberships and sample weights. A partially unfrozen ModernBERT encodes original and masked text; projected CLS and masked-mean features may be combined with style features. Original, masked and bounded correction heads produce the deployed logit, with an optional auxiliary-label head. Training combines weighted BCE losses, consistency and correction penalties, plus identity-stratified subgroup, BPSN and BNSP ranking losses using queues and soft worst-group aggregation. Batches include scheduled subgroup/background anchors. AdamW uses separate backbone and head rates, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Validation restores the best checkpoint; length-sorted inference returns sigmoid probabilities in original order.

title: ModernBERT Attribution-Aware Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes comments, marks URLs, emails and user references, detects quotations, and builds an author-focused view with quoted material removed when sufficient text remains. Train-fitted dense features encode text statistics, style cues, quotation/author proportions, lexical indicators and training-only duplicate frequency. Tokenized author and full-text views are combined and processed by a pretrained ModernBERT encoder. CLS, masked mean/max and learned attention-pooled token states are projected; normalized dense features pass through an MLP and sigmoid gate before fusion. Heads predict toxicity, uncertainty, and masked subtype and identity labels. Training uses weighted soft-label toxicity BCE, uncertainty and auxiliary BCE losses, plus global and identity-group pairwise ranking losses with smooth worst-group aggregation. Stratified batches, AdamW with layer-wise encoder decay, warmup/cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping are used. Inference returns clamped sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Conditional Identity-Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution preprocesses comments into normalized main and heuristically selected focus text, plus 36 standardized and clipped dense style, lexical, toxicity-cue, identity-context, and obfuscation features. A paired-text DeBERTa-v3-large encoder uses frozen embeddings/lower layers and up to eight trainable final layers. CLS, masked-mean, and masked-max pooling are fused with projected dense features through normalized residual layers. Multi-dropout heads predict soft toxicity; optional masked auxiliary labels and identity labels are trained through additional heads. An identity adversary receives gradient-reversed text features and detached toxicity conditioning. The objective combines weighted soft-target BCE, confidence-weighted hard-label BCE, masked positive-weighted auxiliary BCE, and weighted identity BCE. Sampling weights emphasize toxicity/identity subgroups. AdamW uses layer-wise learning-rate decay, separate head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation, and gradient clipping; adversarial strength ramps during early updates. Inference disables adversarial reversal and clips finite sigmoid probabilities to [0,1].

title: Conditional adversarial DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: The system normalizes comment text, derives an obfuscation-normalized focus sentence, and computes 35 dense context, lexical, punctuation, casing, identity and position features. Training-only standardization clips these features. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder, with frozen lower components and trainable upper layers, encodes paired full and focus text. CLS, masked mean and max pooling are projected and residually fused with projected dense features. Dropout-averaged toxicity heads produce a scalar logit; masked auxiliary subtype and conditional identity-adversarial heads are optional. The adversary uses gradient-reversed text features conditioned on detached toxicity probability or target. Loss combines soft-target and confidence-weighted hard-label toxicity BCE, masked class-weighted auxiliary BCE, and masked weighted identity BCE. Samples are reweighted by toxicity and identity-label status. AdamW uses layer-wise encoder rates, AMP, accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Inference disables adversarial training, applies sigmoid and clips probabilities.

title: Counterfactual ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, replaces emails, URLs, IPs and handles with markers, and creates identity-masked counterfactual text. It derives scaled style features and soft/binary toxicity targets, with sample weights emphasizing identity-related cases. A ModernBERT encoder processes original and masked inputs; frozen lower layers retain selected upper layers for training. CLS and masked-mean pooled representations, optionally combined with numeric style features, feed original and masked toxicity heads. The final logit applies a tanh-bounded correction based on both representations. Training combines weighted soft-target BCE for final and branch logits, optional auxiliary supervision, benign-identity consistency, correction regularization, and queued pairwise subgroup/background ranking losses. Batches include fairness-stratum anchors. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, selective weight decay, AMP, accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine scheduling. Inference length-sorts inputs, predicts sigmoid probabilities, and restores input order; checkpoints include model, tokenizer, feature artifacts and manifest.

title: Identity-aware ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: The solution cleans Unicode and HTML text, replaces emails, URLs, IPs and handles, and creates identity-masked counterfactual versions. It derives lexical/style features plus toxicity, auxiliary, identity and weighting metadata. A pretrained ModernBERT encodes original and masked text; selected final layers and normalization parameters are trainable. CLS and masked-mean representations, optionally concatenated with numeric features, feed toxicity and auxiliary heads. The final toxicity logit combines the masked-text logit with a tanh-bounded correction using both views. Training uses weighted soft-target BCE, branch and auxiliary losses, consistency and correction penalties, and pairwise ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN and BNSP comparisons. Four queues retain subgroup/background positive/negative examples; soft worst-group weighting uses ranking availability and queue statistics. Metric-stratified batches include identity/class anchors. Optimization uses AdamW, AMP, accumulation, clipping and warmup-cosine scheduling. Inference length-sorts inputs, applies sigmoid, and restores original order; best checkpoints are evaluated and prediction CSVs written.

title: Counterfactual ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes toxicity comments, replaces contact and web patterns with tokens, constructs identity-masked counterparts, and derives standardized style features. ModernBERT-large encodes original and masked texts; pooled CLS and attention-masked mean representations can be combined with encoded numeric features. Separate toxicity heads score both branches, while a correction network adjusts the masked logit using paired representations. Training uses weighted toxicity and branch BCE losses, consistency loss, subgroup-related ranking losses, optional auxiliary BCE, and correction regularization. Batches jointly tokenize paired text with dynamic padding and include metric-stratified anchors. AdamW uses differential backbone and head rates, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine scheduling. The scheduler advances only after successful optimizer updates. Inference length-sorts inputs, applies sigmoid to logits, and restores original order; validation and test predictions are exported after best-checkpoint restoration.

title: Adversarial DeBERTa and sparse toxicity classifiers
summary: The solution preprocesses comments into normalized paired model/focus text and 36 clipped, standardized lexical-style features. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder pools CLS, masked-mean, and masked-max token states; frozen early layers, projected dense features, residual fusion, and a four-dropout toxicity head produce soft-label predictions. Auxiliary subtype heads and a conditional identity adversary use masked targets; the adversary receives gradient-reversed text features conditioned on detached toxicity probability. Losses combine weighted soft-label and confidence-weighted hard-label BCE, masked class-weighted auxiliary BCE, and weighted identity BCE. Identity-aware sample weighting is normalized and clipped. Training uses paired tokenization, deterministic shuffling, AMP, accumulation, clipping, AdamW layer-wise learning rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, and a ramped adversarial coefficient. A separate hashed word/character n-gram logistic SGD classifier is trained online using positive/negative fractional-label duplication. Inference applies sigmoid or sparse positive-class probabilities, validates finiteness, and clips outputs.

title: Attribution-Aware Gated Transformer Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, masks URLs, emails and user references, separates author text from quotations, and builds 31 train-standardized dense text features. A pretrained ModernBERT encoder receives concatenated author and full-comment text (up to 512 tokens). CLS, masked mean, masked max and attention pooling are projected, gated, and fused with encoded dense features. Heads predict soft toxicity, uncertainty, observed toxicity subtypes and identity labels; identity annotations are targets only. The objective combines weighted BCE for soft toxicity, masked auxiliary BCE losses, and pairwise softplus ranking losses overall and across identity-based subgroup/background strata, with smooth worst-group aggregation. Batches are seeded, no-replacement stratified by binary toxicity class; positives receive higher example weight. Fine-tuning uses AdamW with layer-wise encoder learning-rate decay, higher head rates, warmup and cosine decay, decoupled weight-decay exclusions, clipping, accumulation, mixed precision and optional checkpointing/TF32. Inference returns sigmoid-clamped toxicity probabilities. Checkpoints retain model, tokenizer, encoder configuration and feature state.

title: Fairness-Regularized DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML-normalized; URLs, emails, IPs, mentions and newlines become markers. Train-only identity-term swaps create deterministic counterfactuals. Standardized clipped style features capture text structure, markers and lexical abuse/civility signals. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder pools token sequences into a toxicity representation, which is fused with gated style features and classified by averaged logits from four dropout heads. Optional subtype and identity heads use masked labels; identity prediction receives gradient-reversed representations. The objective combines weighted BCE for soft and hard toxicity targets, masked subtype BCE, adversarial identity BCE, counterfactual Smooth-L1 consistency, and stochastic-pass symmetric Bernoulli-KL. Weights emphasize positives and identity subgroups with subgroup class balancing. Dynamic batches tokenize and pad text and available counterfactuals. AdamW applies layer-wise decayed backbone learning rates and higher head rates, with AMP, accumulation, clipping, cosine warmup scheduling, and a sigmoid adversarial ramp. Inference returns sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Quote-Aware Bias-Weighted Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, marks quotes, URLs, emails and mentions, and creates asserted and quoted text views. It derives 30 standardized, clipped structural features from training-fitted statistics, including training-only duplicate frequency. A ModernBERT-large encoder with added quote-boundary tokens pools full, asserted and quoted token states separately. Dense features and asserted text form a base toxicity logit; a gated bounded quote contribution, informed by quoted, residual and contextual representations, adjusts it. The model predicts toxicity probability, concentration, quote diagnostics and optional subtypes. Training uses clipped soft labels, hard toxicity labels, annotator counts, subtype and identity annotations. Its weighted objective combines beta-binomial likelihood, soft and hard BCE, optional subtype, quote-attribution and concentration terms, with duplicate and identity-based weighting. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, clipping, warmup-cosine scheduling and checkpoint validation. Inference tokenizes dynamically and returns finite clipped sigmoid probabilities.

title: Quote-Aware Bias-Aware Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, identifies quotations, and creates full, asserted, and quoted text views. A train-fitted processor generates standardized, clipped lexical and structural dense features and duplicate-frequency statistics. ModernBERT-large is fine-tuned after adding quote-boundary tokens. Attention pooling separately summarizes lexical tokens, asserted non-quote tokens, and quoted tokens; pooled representations and dense features predict an asserted-content toxicity logit. A quote-presence gate and bounded quote-logit adjustment modify this prediction. The model also outputs a concentration parameter and optional subtype logits. Training uses soft and binary toxicity labels, annotator counts, optional subtype and identity labels, and weighted examples. Its objective combines beta-binomial likelihood, soft and hard BCE, optional subtype BCE, quote attribution, concentration regularization, and identity weighting. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates. Dynamic padded batches use mixed precision, gradient accumulation, clipping, warmup followed by cosine decay, and checkpoint validation. Inference returns clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier with Queue Ranking Loss
summary: The solution normalizes comment text (Unicode NFKC; removal of control characters; URL, email and mention replacement) and extracts 16 style/length features. Toxicity and identity labels are clipped to [0,1], with soft and thresholded hard toxicity targets. Standardized, clipped numeric features are fused with layer-normalized masked-mean ModernBERT-large embeddings through GELU projections, dropout and a single-logit head. Tokenization uses truncation, dynamic padding to multiples of eight and no token-type IDs. Training combines binary cross-entropy on soft targets with a 0.20-weighted queue-backed pairwise softplus ranking loss over overall and identity subgroup/background pair types. The FIFO queue stores detached logits, hard labels and identity masks, sampling up to 512 pairs per direction. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, warmup then exponential decay, selective weight-decay exclusion, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping. Inference batches in order, applies sigmoid, validates finite shapes and clips probabilities. Checkpoints retain model, tokenizer, preprocessing metadata and scaler.

title: Fairness-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classification
summary: Unicode/HTML-normalized comments are anonymized and paired with clipped standardized style features. Selected examples receive deterministic identity-term counterfactuals. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes up to 256 tokens; pooled text representations are transformed and gated with encoded style features to produce dropout-averaged toxicity logits, with optional masked subtype and identity heads. Identity prediction may apply gradient reversal to toxicity features. Training combines weighted soft/hard toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, counterfactual Smooth-L1 consistency, R-Drop Bernoulli-KL, and queue-based pairwise ranking for identity subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP pools. EMA cell losses derive capped fairness weights; pairwise loss ramps after successful optimizer updates. Counterfactual logits are computed in an extra forward pass and inserted into a detached logits copy for the criterion. AdamW uses layer-wise decay, higher head learning rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, AMP, accumulation, clipping, and checkpointing. Evaluation reports overall and identity-family AUCs with negative fifth-power aggregation.

title: Group-Robust ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are NFKC-normalized, stripped of control characters, anonymized for URLs, emails and mentions, and converted into 16 clipped numeric text features. A ModernBERT-large encoder creates masked-mean text embeddings, fused with a two-layer GELU numeric branch to predict a toxicity logit. Clipped soft targets, hard labels and thresholded identity masks support training and ranking. The objective combines soft binary cross-entropy with queue-backed pairwise softplus ranking losses for overall, subgroup, BPSN and BNSP pools. Per-identity loss statistics update EMA-based capped-simplex Group-DRO weights. A deterministic sampler packs identity roles in sampling windows. AdamW uses separate backbone and head rates, selective weight decay, warmup-decay scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping. Non-finite losses are rejected; skipped scaled updates discard pending Group-DRO statistics, while successful updates commit them. Inference batches tokenized text, applies sigmoid and clips outputs.

title: ModernBERT Group-Robust Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode-normalized and sanitized, while 16 style and length features are standardized from training data and clipped. Toxicity and identity annotations are clipped to [0,1], producing soft targets, hard 0.5-threshold targets, and identity masks. A ModernBERT-large encoder generates masked-mean text embeddings; a two-layer GELU branch encodes numeric features, then fusion produces one toxicity logit. Training minimizes soft binary cross-entropy plus weighted queue-backed pairwise ranking losses for overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP pools. A circular queue stores detached logits, labels, and identity masks across batches. Persistent Group-DRO weights are updated from EMA group losses using temperature-scaled exponentiation and capped-simplex projection. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, selective weight decay, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, warm-up and decayed scheduling. Validation combines overall and group AUC measures. Inference tokenizes with dynamic padded truncation, applies sigmoid, and clips probabilities.

title: ModernBERT Group-DRO Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, replaces URLs, emails and mentions, and extracts 16 standardized text-style features. A pretrained ModernBERT encoder yields masked-mean-pooled, layer-normalized text embeddings; a GELU numeric branch embeds engineered features, and a fusion network predicts toxicity. A six-logit subtype head is trained with masked BCE for observed subtype labels, weighted by 0.15. The primary objective combines BCE on clipped soft targets with queue-backed pairwise ranking losses for overall, identity-subgroup, BPSN and BNSP groups. Persistent Group-DRO weights are updated from EMA cell losses after successful optimizer steps using capped-simplex projection. Batches use dynamic, length-limited padding. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates, warmup and exponential decay, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping. Inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities to [0,1]. Checkpoints include model, criterion, tokenizer, feature scaler and processing metadata.

title: Bias-aware hashed toxicity ranker
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML cleaned; URLs, emails, mentions, identity aliases and selected contextual cues are tokenized. Hashed word 1–2 gram and character-within-word 3–5 gram features are combined with scaled numeric lexical, stylistic, cue, identity-window and neutralized-text-frequency features. A sparse EmbeddingBag wide component and LayerNorm–SiLU dense tower produce scaled combined logits. Soft toxicity labels are coerced to [0,1]; identity states distinguish present, absent and unknown. Training uses mean-normalized, clipped bias-aware example weights with weighted soft binary cross-entropy, overall ranking, and subgroup, BPSN and BNSP softplus ranking losses. Pair sides are capped and worse identity groups receive detached softmax emphasis. Adagrad uses separate wide and dense learning rates with gradient clipping. Seeded batches create deduplicated CSR sparse inputs. Inference applies sigmoid, verifies outputs, and clips probabilities. Checkpoints store model, optimizer, feature state, diagnostics and RNG state.

title: Style-Gated Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Text is Unicode/HTML-normalized, with URLs, emails, IPs, user references and newlines replaced by tokens. Train-only identity-word substitutions create deterministic counterfactual texts for selected comments. Clipped standardized lexical/style features capture length, casing, punctuation, references, profanity, civility, pronouns, negation and abuse. A 256-token DeBERTa-v3-large encoder pools text into a toxicity representation; an MLP encodes style features and a learned gate controls their fused contribution. Four dropout toxicity heads are averaged. Optional subtype heads and gradient-reversed identity heads provide masked auxiliary supervision. The objective combines weighted BCE for soft and thresholded toxicity targets, masked subtype and adversarial identity BCE, counterfactual Smooth-L1 consistency, and stochastic-pass symmetric Bernoulli KL. AdamW uses layer-wise backbone learning-rate decay, higher head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping. Inference tokenizes text, computes style features, and outputs sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Bias-aware hashed toxicity ranker
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML normalized; controls, URLs, emails, mentions, and identity aliases are replaced with tokens. Context tokens represent identity, hostility, support, negation, and obfuscated profanity. Features combine L2-normalized hashed word 1–2-grams and within-word character 3–5-grams with lexical, style, identity-context, and text-frequency numeric features standardized on training data. A sparse EmbeddingBag wide component is added to a LayerNorm MLP dense tower with 64 and 24 SiLU units, dropout, learnable branch scales, and bias. Soft toxicity and auxiliary targets are numeric-coerced, imputed, and clipped. Identity-related sample weights are clipped and mean-normalized. Training uses weighted BCE and bounded pairwise ranking losses, emphasizing worse-performing groups. Adagrad updates sparse and dense parameters separately with gradient clipping. Batched inference uses sigmoid probabilities, validates and clips outputs, and checkpoints training and preprocessing state.

title: Bias-aware hashed toxicity classifier
summary: Comments are normalized by Unicode/HTML cleanup, control-text removal, URL/email/mention tokenization, identity-alias replacement, and synthetic context tokens for identity and profanity contexts. L2-normalized hashed word unigrams/bigrams and character-within-word 3–5 grams are combined with 28 lexical, stylistic, identity-context, and training-text-frequency features. Dense features are standardized using training data. Identity annotations create subgroup flags and clipped, normalized bias-aware sample weights. A sparse EmbeddingBag wide branch processes hashed features; a LayerNorm MLP with 64 and 24 SiLU units and dropout processes dense inputs. Scaled branch logits plus bias produce sigmoid probabilities. Training minimizes weighted soft-label binary cross-entropy, pairwise logistic ranking losses for overall and identity-related pair types, softmax-weighted group losses, and logit L2 regularization. Adagrad uses separate sparse/dense parameter groups and gradient clipping. CSR batches are built on demand; evaluation-mode batched inference clips finite probabilities to [0,1]. Checkpoints store model, optimizer, criterion, preprocessing state, configurations, and RNG states.
